hero.filename: Days Before Battle of Droop Mountain.png
hero.caption: This map shows points of interest in the days before the Battle of Droop Mountain that occurred in West Virginia during November 1863. In the battle, Union forces led by Brigadier General William W. Averell defeated a Confederate force led by Brigadier General John Echols and Colonel William L. Jackson.
hero.alt: This map shows points of interest in the days before the Battle of Droop Mountain that occurred in West Virginia during November 1863. In the battle, Union forces led by Brigadier General William W. Averell defeated a Confederate force led by Brigadier General John Echols and Colonel William L. Jackson.
hero.artist: G.W. & C.B. Colton with modifications by TwoScarsUp

images.caption: William Woods Averell (1832–1900) was a United States Army officer and a cavalry general in the American Civil War. After the war he was a diplomat and became wealthy by inventing American asphalt pavement.

images.filename: Skirmish at Mill Point WV Step 2.png
images.caption: The map shows Union and Confederate troop movements leading to a skirmish at Mill Point, West Virginia, on November 5, 1863. Additional troops for both sides fought on the next day 11 miles (18 km) south in the Battle of Droop Mountain. Schoonmaker took the southern route for the Union.  Oley took the west-then-south route. Arnett took the CSA route (red).
images.alt: The map shows Union and Confederate troop movements leading to a skirmish at Mill Point, West Virginia, on November 5, 1863. Additional troops for both sides fought on the next day 11 miles (18 km) south in the Battle of Droop Mountain. Schoonmaker took the southern route for the Union.  Oley took the west-then-south route. Arnett took the CSA route (red).
images.artist: G.W. & C.B. Colton published map in 1876, modifications by TwoScarsUp in 2020

images.caption: This is a United States War Department map of the Droop Mountain battlefield, including positions of the Union and Confederate armies. The Battle occurred on November 6, 1863, with the Union force led by William W. Averell defeating a Confederate Force led by John Echols. The map's orientation is somewhat "upside down", as Hillsborough is actually northeast of Droop Mountain.

images.caption: This is a map that shows the Union troop movements of November 1863 in West Virginia. The plan was to capture Lewisburg and then move south to disable the Virginia & Tennessee Railroad, but the Battle of Droop Mountain happened instead.
images.alt: This is a map that shows the Union troop movements of November 1863 in West Virginia. The plan was to capture Lewisburg and then move south to disable the Virginia & Tennessee Railroad, but the Battle of Droop Mountain happened instead.

images.caption: This is a United States War Department map of the Droop Mountain battlefield, including positions of the Union and Confederate armies. The Battle occurred on November 6, 1863, with the Union force led by William W. Averell defeating a Confederate Force led by John Echols. The map's orientation is somewhat "upside down", as the top of the map is south. The point of view is Averell's (approaching from the north) as the right side of the map is Averell's right and Echols' left.
